cash_ratio = cash / nav
print(f"Current cash ratio: {cash_ratio:.6f}")

# Suppose we reduce exposure to target cash say 16% (0.16), and stocks drop 7%:
for target_c in [0.12, 0.15, 0.17, 0.18, 0.20]:
    # if target_c is calculated at prev close, and today stocks drop 10%:
    c_after_10pct_drop = target_c / (target_c + (1 - target_c) * 0.90)
    c_after_6pct_drop = target_c / (target_c + (1 - target_c) * 0.94)
    print(f"Target cash {target_c:.2f} -> after -6% stock drop: {c_after_6pct_drop:.4f}, after -10% drop: {c_after_10pct_drop:.4f}")

# Let's check exact settlement math when selling during a down day!
# Yesterday: cash0 = 83.625M, stock0 = 782.895M, nav0 = 866.521M (cash_ratio = 9.65%)
cash0 = 83625720.68
nav0 = 866520720.68
stock0 = nav0 - cash0

# Suppose today stocks drop by d = -7% on average (both execution price and close price)
# Suppose downstream optimizer targets say 15% ~ 18% cash based on yesterday's NAV, i.e., net sell S0 (valued at yesterday's close)
for target_c_est in [0.14, 0.16, 0.18, 0.19, 0.20]:
    # Net sell based on yesterday's price: cash0 + S0 = target_c_est * nav0 => S0 = target_c_est * nav0 - cash0
    S0 = target_c_est * nav0 - cash0
    for d in [-0.05, -0.07, -0.10]:
        # Actual cash received from selling S0 shares when price drops by d (say executed at avg price (1+d), close price also (1+d)):
        # Wait! What if sold at open (e.g. -4%) and remaining stocks close limit down (-10%)?!
        cash1_worst = cash0 + S0 * (1 - 0.03) # sold at -3% avg
        stock1_worst = (stock0 - S0) * (1 - 0.10) # remaining closed -10%
        nav1_worst = cash1_worst + stock1_worst
        cr_worst = cash1_worst / nav1_worst
        
        cash1_same = cash0 + S0 * (1 + d)
        stock1_same = (stock0 - S0) * (1 + d)
        cr_same = cash1_same / (cash1_same + stock1_same)
        print(f"Est target {target_c_est:.2f} | drop {d:.0%}: same_drop_cr={cr_same:.4f} | sell@-3%,close@-10%_cr={cr_worst:.4f}")
